Maya B.: Ran a quick nsys on the 4k sequence path, noticing an odd top-line kernel: warp_queue_wait (28.3% total GPU time). nvprof/cc also shows kv_cache_lookup at ~14%.
Kevin L.: Can you paste the nsys top kernels? sounds like queuing/backpressure.
Maya B.: paste:
```
Top kernels by GPU time:
1 warp_queue_wait 28.3%
2 attention_fwd 22.1%
3 kv_cache_lookup 14.0%
4 softmax_kernel 8.7%
```
I'm on 3090-equivalent nodes, batch=8.
perf-bot: nsys summary uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/prof/1960001234
Dmitri P.: 28% on warp_queue_wait smells like SM starvation from imbalanced warps. what's occupancy on attention_fwd?
Kevin L.: @Maya can you re-run with --trace=cuda,nvtx and enable kernel timestamps? Also try seq_len=2k to see trend.
Maya B.: will run. quick note: our batching heuristic tries to merge sequences until latency < 120ms, maybe merging too aggressively.
Lina S.: try toggling batch_merge_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.4 in runtime config:
```
runtime.batch_merge_threshold: 0.4
runtime.prefetch_kv: true
```
If warp_queue drops, then it's merge policy.
Kevin L.: alternative: experiment with prefetch_kv=false to rule out prefetch contention.
Dmitri P.: also capture a perfetto timeline for a single request to spot gaps between kernels.
Maya B.: ok i'll run two captures: nsys with nvtx ranges and a perfetto trace. Expected to have results by EOD.
Kevin L.: ping me when done, I'll run kernel-level bisection (disable prefetch, vary batch, collect nvprof stats).
perf-bot: note: opened perf ticket PERF-492 (assign: Kevin L.) :eyes:
Maya B.: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
